reference.title: Barbell Banded Bench Press
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold it as the bar lowers and touches, breathe out through the top half of the press.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a light touch, about 1.2 s up (bands pull the bar down faster: control it)

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen, usually lighter than your normal bench press, with light to medium bands; leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Heavier bands or more bar weight, one at a time.

cues.text: Loop a band over each sleeve inside the plates and anchor it low on the stands or rack. Shoulder blades back and down, feet planted, grip about 1.5x shoulder width; unrack to straight arms over the shoulders.
Lower under control against the bands to the lower chest, forearms vertical, elbows about 45-60 degrees from the body.
Touch lightly; the bands are slackest here.
Press hard and fast as the bands tighten, up and slightly back over the shoulders; breathe out near the top.
Hold the lockout steady against the bands.

mistakes.fix: Anchor both at the same spot and check the tension is equal before unracking.
Control the lowering; do not let the bands slam the bar into the chest.
Keep them about 45-60 degrees from the trunk.
Keep the buttocks on the bench and drive through the feet.

kinematics.setup: 78 cm between the handle centres (≈2.0x the shoulder joints)
kinematics.norm: About 1.5x shoulder width; wide and medium grips load the chest more than narrow ones (Saeterbakken 2021)

kinematics.peak: ≈116° with the bar on the chest; elbows ≈56° from the trunk
kinematics.norm: About 90 degrees or more at the chest (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Top: over the shoulder joints, 59 cm above the bench
kinematics.peak: Bottom: lower chest, 16 cm toward the feet from the shoulder joints; 35.7 cm of travel
kinematics.norm: From the lower chest up and slightly back over the shoulders (common coaching)

kinematics.setup: Looped over each sleeve (28 cm outside the hands), anchored on the stands' base rails 3 cm off the floor
kinematics.peak: Band length 68.9 cm with the bar on the chest to 101.5 cm at lockout (+47%)
kinematics.norm: Band tension adds resistance toward lockout (accommodating resistance; common coaching)

kinematics.peak: 2 s down, 0.3 s touch, 1.2 s up, 0.7 s at the top

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Banded Bench Press, video (movement reference only)

Saeterbakken, Stien, Pedersen, Solstad, Cumming and Andersen 2021, the effect of grip width on muscle strength and electromyographic activity in bench press among novice- and resistance-trained men (Int J Environ Res Public Health 18(12):6444; PMC8296276)

cautions: Press with a spotter or inside a rack with safeties; bands make the bar harder to re-rack.
Check the bands for nicks and that the anchors cannot slip before every set.
Unrack and re-rack with the bands already tensioned; move the bar slowly.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder pain: lighter bands, shorter range (floor press), narrower grip.
No anchors available: use chains or skip the bands.
